method_limits: the parent is a string prefix of the composed key, not a filesystem question: a parent that a `..` segment or a glob pattern defeats is graded as if it were literal

resolution only follows a string literal or a module-level constant of the same file; a parent built from a parameter, a temp dir or a config read is published as parent_not_resolvable and is never counted as an orphan

superseded means 'some open in this file lands under that parent' -- it does not mean the intended artifact exists; the basis column separates an exact re-open of the same path from a sibling open, and a file that writes many artifacts under one parent will mark every drop there as superseded
openers are recognised by a frozen tail vocabulary (open/read_*/write_*/to_*/load/dump/mkdir/remove/...); an opener reached through an alias (`op = open`) is not in it
a text join is only excluded when the receiver is a string constant; `sep.join(...)` on a variable receiver is still read as a path composition
static only: nothing is executed, so an open performed inside a helper called from this file is invisible here
